title: Disc Stack Centrifuge

introduction.definition: A disc stack centrifuge (separator) spins a bowl at thousands of rpm. Inside, a stack of conical discs splits the liquid into thin layers so that particles and droplets only need to travel a short distance to separate. Heavier phases move outwards; lighter liquid moves inwards and leaves at the top. Collected solids are ejected periodically.
applications: Fuel and lube-oil purification (ships, power plants)
key_points: Discs give a large equivalent settling area
introduction.summary: A disc stack centrifuge separates liquids of different density and fine solids from liquids at very high g-force. A stack of conical discs inside the fast-spinning bowl splits the flow into thin layers, so particles settle a very short distance. Solids collect at the bowl wall and are ejected periodically.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Separation capacity ∝ equivalent clarifying area Σ; throughput falls for finer particles.

pressure.title: Centrifugal force: thousands of g
pressure.description: At a few thousand rpm the bowl generates several thousand times gravity (g-force = ω²r/g). Heavier solids and liquid move outwards to the bowl wall (red, the sludge space); the discs split the flow into thin layers so particles only have a short distance to settle. Accumulated solids are ejected periodically by opening the bowl.

video_tutorials.title: Disc Stack Centrifuge — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Disc Stack Centrifuge.
A disc stack centrifuge (separator) spins a bowl at thousands of rpm.
Inside, a stack of conical discs splits the liquid into thin layers so that particles and droplets only need to travel a short distance to separate.
Heavier phases move outwards; lighter liquid moves inwards and leaves at the top.
Typical applications include milk skimming and clarification; fuel and lube-oil purification (ships, power plants); beer, wine and juice clarification; biotech and pharma.

The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Frame (with solids collector) & Hood, Bowl with Disc Stack & Distributor (rotates ≈ 4 000–10 000 rpm), Bowl Lock Ring & Discharge Ports (turn with the bowl), Vertical Spindle & Bearings (with damping springs).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Disc Stack Centrifuge — Operation

script.narration: How the Disc Stack Centrifuge works.
Feed enters down the central pipe into the distributor.
The bowl and discs spin at high speed.
Heavy phase and solids move outward along the discs.
Light phase moves inward and is pumped out by the paring disc.
Solids are ejected through the ports at intervals.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
At a few thousand rpm the bowl generates several thousand times gravity (g-force = ω²r/g).

video_tutorials.title: Disc Stack Centrifuge — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Disc Stack Centrifuge.
Monitor vibration, speed, outlet pressure.
Inspect and clean disc stack.
Bowl overhaul and balancing; spindle bearings.
Watch for vibration: high vibration trip. Common cause: unbalanced bowl (uneven solids), worn bearings.
Watch for poor separation: cloudy light phase. Common cause: too high flow, wrong gravity disc.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
